tema: Evaluates the synergy of pharmacological-dose ascorbate with ceftriaxone against Staphylococcus aureus and its effect on the bactericidal activity of macrophages.
diseno: In vitro experimental study (time-kill assays with ATCC strains of S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, A. baumannii and E. coli, bone marrow macrophages) and a murine model of S. aureus myositis, including MRSA.
hallazgos: There was bactericidal synergy of ascorbate (10 and 40 mM) plus ceftriaxone against S. aureus, but not other bacteria. Ascorbate alone enhanced macrophage activity and eliminated bacteria at high concentrations; the combination reduced bacterial load and cytokines in the myositis model, also with MRSA.
conclusion: Ascorbate-ceftriaxone synergy against S. aureus is demonstrated; the time-kill assay could serve to select patients who would benefit from adjuvant therapy.
triangulacion: Full coherence: the conclusions come from the abstract and the keywords agree. The study does not deal with ME/CFS, so its inclusion in the topic is tangential.

tema: Evaluates daytime HRV parameters as a biomarker in CFS/ME and their relationship to self-reported symptoms.
diseno: Case-control study with 45 women with CFS/ME (CDC/Fukuda 1994 criteria) and 25 matched controls; recording of RR intervals in three 5-min periods with mHealth technology; time- and frequency-domain analysis; correlation and linear regression.
hallazgos: Patients scored higher on all questionnaires, with shorter RR intervals and lower HRV parameters (except LF/HF). Self-reported fatigue was related to mean RR, RMSSD and HFnu in patients, but not in controls.
conclusion: Autonomic dysfunction, such as sympathetic hyperactivity, could contribute to fatigue severity, and HRV by mHealth would be useful for predicting it; larger, longitudinal cohorts, including men, are required.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions broaden the proposed use (monitoring to prevent PEM, two-day CPET, HPA axis), beyond what was evaluated.

tema: Explores the opinions of participants with ME/CFS and multiple sclerosis from the UK ME/CFS Biobank on the findings, dissemination and priorities of biomedical research.
diseno: Qualitative study with five focus groups at two UK sites; 28 participants (16 with ME/CFS, 12 with MS); thematic analysis.
hallazgos: Five themes emerged: search for coherence, for acceptance (stigma and validation), for diagnosis, for a better future and for sharing knowledge. Progress was perceived as 'putting together a jigsaw puzzle' through perseverance and collaboration.
conclusion: Research has great emotional, social and practical importance for patients; their voices should guide biomedical research toward a more collaborative culture.
triangulacion: High coherence: the keywords (stigma, diagnosis, patient participation) reflect the themes; the conclusions come from the abstract itself, so they provide no independent triangulation.

tema: Explores the relationship between oxidative stress, exercise-induced pain and parasympathetic activity in ME/CFS versus inactive healthy controls.
diseno: Observational secondary analysis of 36 women (ME/CFS patients and healthy controls); submaximal exercise test with cardiorespiratory monitoring, TBARS as a measure of oxidative stress, heart rate variability and pain visual analogue scale.
hallazgos: Pain differed between groups before and after exercise and only improved after exercise in controls. Oxidative stress did not change with exercise; TBARS correlated with pain in patients (r=0.540 baseline; r=0.524 post-exercise). In controls, more parasympathetic activity was associated with a greater reduction in oxidative stress.
conclusion: Vagal activity could regulate oxidative stress during exercise; ME/CFS patients may lack this control, which would explain the absence of exercise-induced hypoalgesia.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The abstract is truncated; the conclusions add the interpretation of vagal control and acknowledge the limitation of using indirect measures.

tema: Examines the effect of an individualized activity programme (IAP) on cardiovascular, mitochondrial, autonomic and fatigue parameters in CFS.
diseno: Intervention study without a control group: 34 patients completed 16 weeks of IAP; CFQ, FSS and FIS; CPET (peak VO2, submaximal VO2, heart rate); plasma Mfn1 and Mfn2; Task Force Monitor at rest and on the tilt table.
hallazgos: Fatigue scores decreased and Mfn1 and Mfn2 increased (p = 0.002 and p = 0.00005). Relationships were observed between peak VO2 and the increase in Mfn1 (p = 0.03) and between VO2 at anaerobic threshold and the autonomic response to the tilt table (p = 0.03).
conclusion: The IAP reduces fatigue and improves functional performance together with autonomic and mitochondrial changes, although with caution because 51% of patients did not tolerate exercise well.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions come from the structured abstract and reproduce it. The poor tolerance in half of the patients qualifies the positive message.

tema: Synthesizes the 24-h test-retest changes in VO2 and workload in repeated maximal tests between ME/CFS and controls.
diseno: Systematic review with a search in seven databases, observational studies in adults with ME/CFS versus healthy individuals; quality with SAQOR; random-effects meta-analysis.
hallazgos: The decrease in peak workload on the second test was greater in ME/CFS by 8.55 W (five studies) and at the anaerobic threshold by 21 W (four studies); 78% probability that a future study exceeds the minimal clinically important difference of 10 W.
conclusion: People with ME/CFS show a clinically significant reduction in workload at the anaerobic threshold on the second test, which supports a possible physiological mechanism.
triangulacion: The three sources agree. The conclusions are cautious (they speak of possible evidence) and propose exploring the minimum demand that triggers the response.

tema: Evaluates the effect of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) on the symptoms of ME patients.
diseno: Uncontrolled intervention study in 30 ME patients (7 men, 23 women); rTMS of the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and primary motor area; before-after comparison of functional status, OI on standing test, imbalance, pain and strength.
hallazgos: 67% improved by at least 2 points in functional status; OI resolved in 10 of 12 patients, imbalance in 15 of 17 and neuropathic pain or fibromyalgia eased in 7 of 10. There were no adverse effects.
conclusion: rTMS would be effective in relieving symptoms, especially OI and imbalance, and should be considered a therapeutic option.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions reinforce the thesis of imbalance as a cause of OI. No source mentions a control group, which limits claims of efficacy.

tema: Documents the test-retest variability of CPET in two ME/CFS patients versus other conditions with fatigue.
diseno: Case series of 6 women matched for age and BMI (sedentary, active, multiple sclerosis, HIV and two with ME/CFS) with two maximal CPETs 24 h apart.
hallazgos: Participants without disability and with MS and HIV reproduced or improved VO2, workload, HR and ventilation at VAT and peak (except some measures in HIV); no ME/CFS patient reproduced the values at VAT.
conclusion: CPET measures in individual patients can reflect cardiac, pulmonary and metabolic deficits specific to each condition.
triangulacion: The conclusions come from the abstract itself and are identical to it; consistent with the keywords. It is a very small series and the conclusions are cautious.

tema: Compares the response to a two-day CPET between men with ME/CFS and men with idiopathic chronic fatigue (ICF).
diseno: Comparative study with 25 men with ICF and 26 with ME/CFS matched for age and sex; VO2, HR, blood pressure, workload and RER at peak and ventilatory threshold.
hallazgos: ME/CFS patients worsened on the second CPET in VO2 and workload at peak and ventilatory threshold, whereas ICF patients improved with no significant change in peak workload.
conclusion: The reduction in exercise capacity on the second day is confirmed in men with ME/CFS; ICF responds like sedentary controls and could respond to training.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent and replicate the study in women (id 170). The conclusions add, cautiously (could), that ICF would respond to training and ME/CFS would not.

tema: Explores the relationship between cardiovascular autonomic regulation, heart rate response, EtCO2 and severity of orthostatic symptoms and fatigue in chronic orthostatic intolerance.
diseno: Study in 108 patients referred for chronic orthostatic intolerance; standardized Autonomic Reflex Screen, COMPASS-31 and Fatigue Severity Scale.
hallazgos: Greater OI severity was associated with younger age, greater amplitude of Valsalva phase IV and lower adrenergic baroreflex sensitivity. Greater fatigue was associated with a greater EtCO2 decrease on the tilt test and lower LF power of heart variability.
conclusion: Baroreflex and EtCO2 changes are more associated with symptom severity than the heart rate response; non-pharmacological treatments such as heart rate variability biofeedback are proposed, pending study.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree; the discussion adds the focus on biofeedback, absent from the other sources, and calls for larger samples. It contains noise from acknowledgements and declarations.

tema: Shows the change in cerebral hypometabolism on 18F-FDG PET in a post-mononucleosis CFS patient treated with hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT).
diseno: Case report (image of the month) of a 31-year-old man with CFS of 15 months after EBV mononucleosis; 50 HBOT sessions over 6 weeks; 18F-FDG PET/CT before and after, compared using SPM with 20 healthy controls.
hallazgos: The baseline PET showed extensive cerebral hypometabolism which, according to the title, reversed after HBOT treatment.
conclusion: The authors suggest that 18F-FDG PET can serve to evaluate brain dysfunction in indications for HBOT in functional disorders and to assess the therapeutic effect.
triangulacion: Keywords and opening text are consistent, but the available text is cut off before describing the results after HBOT and the discussion is almost all affiliations and ethical declarations; the reversibility is supported mainly by the title and is a single case.

tema: Reviews the anatomy and physiology of the midbrain ascending arousal system nuclei and their implications for ME/CFS, Gulf War illness (GWI) and PEM.
diseno: Narrative review motivated by previous fMRI data in a two-day PEM model.
hallazgos: After exercise, ME/CFS increased dorsal midbrain activation and GWI reduced it. The midbrain nuclei participate in threat, attention, mood, cognition, pain, sleep, thermoregulation, sensitivity to light and sound, orthostatic symptoms and autonomic dysfunction.
conclusion: These nuclei probably contribute to PEM; the review does not presuppose that the lesions are primary and notes that ME/CFS and GWI have different exercise-induced mechanisms.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on midbrain, PEM and GWI; the conclusions clarify that it is not a unifying hypothesis and mention the energy and perfusion vulnerability of the region.

tema: Reanalyses IgG antibody reactivity against EBV antigens to assess its potential as a diagnostic biomarker for ME/CFS.
diseno: Reanalysis of microarray data of IgG against 3054 EBV antigens in 92 ME/CFS patients and 50 healthy controls, using binary regression models with age and sex interactions.
hallazgos: In the overall set, no antibodies discriminated patients and controls. Restricted to patients with probable infectious onset, stronger responses were found against EBNA4_0529 and EBNA6_0070; the model with age and sex reached sensitivity 0.833 and specificity 0.720.
conclusion: Antibody levels against these epitopes could be biomarkers in the infectious-onset subgroup, pending confirmation in an independent cohort.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent around EBV serology and diagnosis; the discussion text contains only ethics approval, contributions and funding, so the conclusion depends on the abstract, which already announces the need for validation.

tema: Investigates whether atopy and allergic rhinitis are more prevalent in CFS and characterizes the rhinitis and systemic symptoms.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with 51 CFS patients, 34 healthy individuals, 27 with allergic rhinitis and 17 with other rheumatological diseases; questionnaires on respiratory and systemic symptoms and allergy skin tests.
hallazgos: Skin tests were positive in 35% of CFS and 44% of healthy individuals (non-significant difference). There was significant rhinitis in 83% and 76% of CFS with positive and negative tests, versus 23% of healthy individuals; the systemic symptom score discriminated CFS from healthy individuals.
conclusion: Atopy does not appear to be increased in CFS; at least 46% have non-allergic rhinitis, whose mechanism could also be involved in the other systemic complaints.
triangulacion: Abstract and discussion are consistent on non-allergic rhinitis; however, the recorded title ('Clinical symptoms in the CFS', 1991) and the generic keywords do not match the text, which corresponds to a study on rhinitis in CFS.

tema: Examines whether serum rituximab concentrations and anti-drug antibodies (ADA) are associated with the clinical response to B cell depletion in ME/CFS.
diseno: Retrospective analysis of samples from 23 of 28 patients (Canadian criteria) in an open-label phase II trial with maintenance rituximab (KTS-2-2010).
hallazgos: There were no differences in rituximab concentrations between 14 patients who improved and 9 who did not. Women had higher concentrations at 3 months and there was a negative correlation between baseline B cells and concentration at 3 months (r = -0.47); no patient developed ADA.
conclusion: Clinical improvement was not related to rituximab concentrations or to ADA, in line with a recent randomized trial that questions the efficacy of rituximab in ME/CFS.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions frame the study as complementary and as a contribution to the search for mechanisms, without claiming efficacy.

tema: Reviews the neuropathology and neurological manifestations of ME/CFS and long COVID, with a focus on post-exertional symptom exacerbation (PESE).
diseno: Literature review (apparently an academic paper with a popular summary). No sample stated.
hallazgos: ME/CFS is associated with CNS abnormalities also proposed for long COVID: neuroinflammation, reduced brain volume, cerebral hypoperfusion and cerebrospinal fluid alterations. In ME/CFS, exercise appears to increase the neural resources needed to perform tasks.
conclusion: Both diseases share symptoms and neuropathology, so the findings could apply to long COVID with PESE; more research and therapeutic approaches tailored to subgroups are needed.
triangulacion: There are no keywords. Abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions add the proposal of an exertion-neuropathology cycle and the need to treat subgroups, maintaining a cautious tone.

tema: Analyses cardiopulmonary and metabolic responses in a two-day CPET in ME/CFS and translates them into disability status and therapeutic considerations.
diseno: Case-control study with 84 ME/CFS patients (Canadian Criteria) and 71 sedentary controls; two CPETs 24 h apart; ANOVA, intraclass correlations; 55 pairs matched for aerobic capacity, age and sex.
hallazgos: Only ME/CFS reduced peak VO2 and other parameters on CPET-2; stability between tests was greater in controls. The abnormalities persisted compared with controls matched for aerobic capacity, with ventilatory inefficiency at VAT and a worse degree of disability according to CPET-2.
conclusion: It is the largest two-day CPET study confirming impaired recovery; fitness does not explain exercise intolerance and autonomic dysregulation of blood flow and oxygenation is implicated.
triangulacion: The three sources agree; the abstract is partially truncated in the results. The PDF conclusions add the reduction in VAT as a contraction of the energy envelope and that many inactive controls also met disability criteria.

tema: Studies arterial lactate accumulation during repeated CPETs at 24 h in women with ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study with 18 women with ME/CFS (Canadian Criteria) and 15 healthy women; two CPETs 24 h apart with arterial lactate every 30 s.
hallazgos: Peak VO2 was lower in patients and decreased on CPET2, although the change did not differ between groups. Lactate per power was higher in patients and increased from CPET1 to CPET2, whereas it decreased in controls; VO2 and power at the gas exchange threshold fell in patients.
conclusion: Prior exercise worsens performance and increases lactate during exercise in ME/CFS, unlike in healthy individuals; whether it is a central or secondary mechanism is unknown.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The discussion adds caution about the mechanism and mentions that patients suffered symptom exacerbation for weeks after the tests.

tema: Perspective article reviewing the history of ME/CFS and comparing it with that of HIV/AIDS to identify what is needed to achieve a similar level of care.
diseno: Narrative review/comparative historical perspective; no primary data.
hallazgos: ME/CFS, described since 1934, still has no cause or diagnostic test; it has been stigmatized as psychosomatic, with scarce research and care. The 2015 IOM report declared it a disease affecting up to 2.5 million Americans.
conclusion: Knowing what has not worked for ME/CFS and what did work for HIV/AIDS can help a severely underserved community.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree on stigma, history and funding. The conclusions, taken from the discussion, include noise (author's note, acknowledgements) and are more cautious and lesson-oriented than the abstract.

tema: Analyses the correlation between autoantibodies against vasoregulatory G protein-coupled receptors (GPCR) and symptom severity, autonomic dysfunction and disability in ME/CFS.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with measurement of autoantibodies by ELISA and questionnaires on severity, symptoms and autonomic dysfunction; the sample size appears truncated in the abstract ('= 116' is read).
hallazgos: In patients with infectious onset, most autoantibodies correlated with fatigue and muscle pain; cognitive impairment correlated with anti-AT1-R and anti-ETA-R autoantibodies, and gastrointestinal symptoms with anti-alpha1/2-AdR. In non-infectious onset there were fewer and different correlations.
conclusion: The correlations of specific anti-GPCR autoantibodies with symptoms support a role of these autoantibodies or of their receptor pathways in the disease mechanism.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusion (taken from the abstract) agree; the conclusion is identical to that of the abstract and the methods section is incomplete in the source.

tema: Develops and validates a nanoelectronic impedance assay in blood as a possible diagnostic biomarker of ME/CFS.
diseno: Development of a multiplex nanoelectronic array to measure biomolecular interactions in real time, tested in patients with moderate to severe ME/CFS and healthy controls under hyperosmotic stress; supervised machine learning classifier; sample size not stated.
hallazgos: The response of ME/CFS samples to the hyperosmotic stressor showed a characteristic impedance pattern very different from that of controls; a classifier capable of identifying new patients was developed.
conclusion: The authors believe that the robust difference in impedance modulation under hyperosmotic stress could provide a unique indicator of ME/CFS and a point-of-care diagnostic tool.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent on blood biomarker, impedance biosensor and machine learning; no conclusions are available, so triangulation is partial.

tema: Critical commentary and preliminary reanalysis of recovery rates after GET and CBT in the PACE trial.
diseno: Secondary reanalysis of published PACE trial data using normative data and the definition of recovery specified in the original protocol.
hallazgos: None of the changes in the recovery criteria was justified; with the final definition one could score below the entry threshold and count as recovered. With the original protocol, recovery was 4% (GET), 7% (CBT) and 3% (control), with no significant differences.
conclusion: The claim that patients recover with CBT and GET is not justified by the data and is misleading for clinicians and patients.
triangulacion: The three sources are fully consistent (PACE, definition of recovery, adherence to the protocol); the conclusions come from the abstract, with no independent source.

tema: Examines whether the circulating cytokine profile or cardiovascular tests after exercise differentiate ME/CFS patients from sedentary controls.
diseno: Case-control study with 24 ME/CFS patients and 24 matched sedentary controls; echocardiography, cardiopulmonary exercise test and endothelial function; Luminex panel of 51 cytokines and growth factors at baseline and 18 h post-exercise; sPLS-DA discriminant analysis.
hallazgos: Cardiac structure and exercise capacity were similar between groups. The cytokine profile 18 h post-exercise offered the best discrimination (κ = 0.62), with CD40L, platelet activating factor inhibitor, IL-1β, interferon-α and CXCL1 as the most discriminating.
conclusion: The cytokine profile after exercise could help differentiate ME/CFS patients from sedentary controls.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; the conclusions extracted from the discussion are only noise (abbreviations and statistical methods), so they provide no useful triangulation.

tema: Reviews the similarities between post-acute COVID-19 symptoms and post-infectious ME/CFS and whether COVID-19 can be its trigger.
diseno: Narrative review of published literature. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Many post-COVID symptoms (fatigue, exercise intolerance, sleep disturbances, concentration problems) resemble ME/CFS, which has been associated with EBV, Q fever, influenza and other coronaviruses; the severity of the acute phase does not clearly correlate with persistent symptoms.
conclusion: There is not enough evidence to establish COVID-19 as a trigger of ME/CFS; longer follow-up, clear diagnostic criteria and studies of risk factors and prevalence are required.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent and cautious; the discussion adds that it will be difficult to separate the effect of pandemic stress from that of the infection and recommends prolonged surveillance and screening for comorbidities.

tema: Pilot study examining cytokines in the cerebrospinal fluid of CFS/ME patients.
diseno: Pilot case-control study with CSF from 18 CFS/ME patients and 5 healthy controls; Bio-Plex assay of 27 cytokines.
hallazgos: Of the 27 cytokines examined, only IL-10 was significantly reduced in patients compared with controls.
conclusion: This preliminary research suggests that alterations in inflammatory cytokines in the CSF could contribute to the neurological abnormalities of CFS/ME.
triangulacion: The three sources agree (conclusions taken from the abstract); there is some discrepancy because the conclusion speaks of inflammatory cytokines when the only finding was the decrease of the anti-inflammatory IL-10, and the neuroinflammation keyword goes beyond the data.
